tldr: IntersectionZoo is a comprehensive benchmark suite for multi-agent contextual reinforcement learning (CRL) built on cooperative eco-driving in urban road networks, using 16,334 signalized intersections from 10 US cities to generate one million data-driven traffic scenarios.
contributions: Introduces IntersectionZoo, a real-world application-grounded benchmark for multi-agent CRL
Provides one million data-driven traffic scenarios based on 16,334 signalized intersections from 10 major US cities
Demonstrates that popular multi-agent RL algorithms struggle to generalize in CRL settings
methods: The authors build IntersectionZoo using data-informed simulations of 16,334 signalized intersections from 10 major US cities, modeled in the SUMO microscopic traffic simulator. Factors affecting vehicular emissions (temperature, road conditions, travel demand) are used to generate approximately one million traffic scenarios organized into 10 context-MDPs. The benchmark uses neural emission models replicating MOVES and Intelligent Driver Models for HDV behavior, with vehicles controlled decentrally to minimize fleet-level exhaust emissions while minimizing travel time impact.
results: Popular multi-agent RL algorithms struggle to generalize in CRL settings. The benchmark provides both IID and OOD evaluation protocols across 10 city-based CMDPs. Existing benchmarks were assessed against 11 key properties for CRL benchmarking, with IntersectionZoo satisfying all properties including realistic task, data-driven context distribution, native CRL support, and multiple objective variations.
limitations: The paper notes that generalization across a full-traffic network remains impractical in large cities and an open optimization challenge; the benchmark decomposes networks into individual intersections with the assumption that vehicle flow is not at saturation. Additionally, CRL focus is limited to intra-task generalization, not inter-task generalization.
